claim: The United States CF Foundation newborn screening consensus guideline states seven program practice recommendations, including floating IRT cutoffs, 95% sensitivity across ancestral groups, expanding beyond F508del and ACMG-23 panels, screening CFTR2 CF-causing variants twice weekly, adding a CFTR sequencing tier, and notifying primary care providers and CF specialists.
quote: Systematic reviews were used to develop seven recommendations for newborn screening program practices to improve timeliness, sensitivity, and equity in diagnosing infants with CF:
The CF Foundation recommends the use of a floating immunoreactive trypsinogen (IRT) cutoff over a fixed IRT cutoff
variant panel that achieves at least 95% sensitivity in all ancestral groups
should not limit CFTR variant detection to the F508del variant or variants included in the American College of Medical Genetics-23 panel
screen for all CF-causing CFTR variants in CFTR2
conducting CFTR variant screening twice weekly or more frequently
The CF Foundation recommends the inclusion of a CFTR sequencing tier following IRT and CFTR variant panel testing
the primary care provider and the CF specialist be notified of abnormal newborn screening results.
scope: Checked in the CC BY 4.0 abstract of McGarry et al. 2025 (PMC12015897).

claim: The ENVISION cystic fibrosis clinical trial consent project produced the four-component RIVER framework (Relationship, Information, Values Exploration, Resolution) backed by two 2-hour training sessions for research coordinators.
quote: The ENgaging with Values to Inform research enrollment deciSIONs (ENVISION) study was launched to improve
making within the context of a multisite cystic fibrosis clinical trial.
The development process resulted in a four-component, values-oriented communication framework, the RIVER framework:
Relationship (forming a connection with the prospective participant), Information (sharing about the study), Values Exploration (eliciting and examining relevant values),
Resolution (confirming a values-aligned decision).
The training curriculum consists of two 2-hour sessions that include didactic teaching, group discussion, and role-play scenarios,
scope: Checked in the CC BY 4.0 abstract of Kraft et al. 2026 (PMC13721633).

claim: Barilla et al. (2026) evaluated targeted CRISPR/Cas9 integration of a partial CFTR exons 2-27 cDNA donor into CFTR intron 1 (TI-1) via integrase-defective lentivirus in CF primary airway basal stem cells and differentiated airway epithelium.
quote: Barilla et al. (2026, DOI 10.1016/j.omtn.2026.103123, PMC13717110) targeted integration of CFTR 2-27 sequence into CFTR intron 1 (TI-1):
we sought to develop a correction methodology utilizing targeted integration of CFTR 2-27 sequence into CFTR intron 1 (TI-1).
Following electroporation of CF primary airway basal stem cells with intron 1-targeted Cas9/gRNA, we delivered CFTR 2-27 donor,
via an integrase defective lentiviral vector.
Fully differentiated airway epithelium, derived from TI-1 treated basal cells without enrichment for corrected cells, exhibited functional restoration of CFTR channel activity
scope: Preclinical airway basal stem cell model read in the CC BY 4.0 abstract of PMC13717110; not a clinical efficacy claim.
